questions.stem:
George throws a ball at a target 15 times.
Each time George throws the ball, the probability of the ball hitting the target is 0.48

The random variable $X$ represents the number of times George hits the target in 15 throws.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find
(i) $\mathrm{P}(X=3)$
(ii) $\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 5)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $X \sim \mathrm{B}(15, 0.48)$ M1
(i) $\mathrm{P}(X=3) = 0.019668\ldots$ awrt 0.0197 A1
(ii) $\left[\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 5) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 4)\right] = 0.92013\ldots$ awrt 0.920 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (ii) A1: awrt 0.920 (Allow 0.92)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
George now throws the ball at the target 250 times.
(b) Use a normal approximation to calculate the probability that he will hit the target more than 110 times.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $Y$ is the number of hits, $M$ is the number of misses
$Y \sim \mathrm{N}(120, 62.4)$; $M \sim \mathrm{N}(130, 62.4)$ B1
$\mathrm{P}(X>110) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y>110.5) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z > \dfrac{110.5-"120"}{\sqrt{"62.4"}}\right)$ or $\mathrm{P}(X>110) \approx \mathrm{P}(M<139.5) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z < \dfrac{139.5-"130"}{\sqrt{"62.4"}}\right)$ M1
$= 0.88544\ldots$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1: Setting up a correct Normal model. Allow sight of $\mathrm{N}(120,62.4)$ or $\mathrm{N}(130,62.4)$ or $\mathrm{N}\left(120,\frac{312}{5}\right)$ or $\mathrm{N}\left(130,\frac{312}{5}\right)$ or may be awarded if used correctly in standardisation or in words: Normal with mean = 120/130 and variance = 62.4 or sd = $\sqrt{62.4}$ condone $\mathrm{N}(120,\sqrt{62.4})$ or $\mathrm{N}(130,\sqrt{62.4})$ or sd = 62.4. Look out for $\sigma=\frac{\sqrt{1560}}{5}$ or $\frac{2\sqrt{390}}{5}$ or awrt 7.90 (condone 7.9). This may be implied by sight of 0.897 or 0.8854…
- M1: Sight of the continuity correction with a normal distribution: 110.5 or 111.5 or 109.5 / 139.5 or 140.5 or 138.5. NB we will also allow 129.5 or 130.5 or 128.5 / NB we will also allow 120.5 or 119.5 or 121.5. Continuity correction may be seen in standardisation. NB No continuity correction(CC) gives awrt 0.897 which is M0 unless CC seen
- A1: awrt 0.8854 or awrt 0.885 dependent on sight of >110.5 or <129.5 or < 139.5 or >120.5. Allow $\leqslant$ or $\geqslant$ instead of < or >. NB 0.885548… from B(250, 0.48) scores M0A0

questions.stem:
A manufacturer uses a machine to make metal rods.
The length of a metal rod, $L\,\mathrm{cm}$, is normally distributed with

$\bullet$ a mean of $8\,\mathrm{cm}$
$\bullet$ a standard deviation of $x\,\mathrm{cm}$

Given that the proportion of metal rods less than $7.902\,\mathrm{cm}$ in length is 2.5%

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $x = 0.05$ to 2 decimal places.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\left[\mathrm{P}(L<7.902)=0.025 \Rightarrow\right] \dfrac{7.902-8}{x} = -1.96$ oe M1
$[x=]0.05$* A1cso*
SC B1 (mark as M0A1) for $\dfrac{7.902-8}{0.05} = -1.96 \Rightarrow 0.024998$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Using the normal distribution to set up equation. Allow $\sigma$ for $x$ and awrt $\pm1.96$. A1*: cso For a correct expression for $x$ followed by 0.05 or 0.05000… No incorrect working seen

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Calculate the proportion of metal rods that are between $7.94\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $8.09\,\mathrm{cm}$ in length.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $\mathrm{P}(7.94 \leqslant L \leqslant 8.09) = 0.8490\ldots$ awrt 0.849 B1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The cost of producing a single metal rod is 20p

A metal rod

$\bullet$ where $L<7.94$ is sold for scrap for 5p
$\bullet$ where $7.94 \leqslant L \leqslant 8.09$ is sold for 50p
$\bullet$ where $L>8.09$ is shortened for an extra cost of 10p and then sold for 50p

(c) Calculate the expected profit per 500 of the metal rods.
Give your answer to the nearest pound.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $[\mathrm{P}(L<7.94)=]0.115069\ldots$ (awrt 0.115) or $[\mathrm{P}(L>8.09)=]0.03593\ldots$ (awrt 0.036) B1
$[\mathrm{P}(L<7.94)=]0.115069\ldots$ (awrt 0.115) & $[\mathrm{P}(L>8.09)=]0.03593\ldots$ (awrt 0.036) B1
Expected income per 500 rods $= \sum(\text{Income} \times \text{probability} \times 500)$
$(500 \times "0.849" \times 0.5) + (500 \times "0.1150\ldots" \times 0.05) + (500 \times "0.03593\ldots" \times 0.4)$ or
Expected profit per rod $= \sum(\text{Profit} \times \text{probability})$
$0.30 \times "0.849" + -0.15 \times "0.1150\ldots" + 0.20 \times "0.03593\ldots" [=0.2446\ldots]$ M1
Expected profit per 500 rods
$500 \times \sum(\text{Profit} \times \text{probability})$ or $500 \times "0.2446\ldots"$ or $"222.3" - 500 \times 0.2$
$= [£]122.3\ldots$ M1d
$=$ awrt $[£]122$ A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1: awrt 0.115 (Implied by awrt 57.5 for number of rods) or awrt 0.036 (Implied by awrt 18 for number of rods). B1: awrt 0.115 (Implied by awrt 57.5 for number of rods) and awrt 0.036 (Implied by awrt 18 for number of rods)
- M1: Correct method to find the total income of 500 rods. Attempt at all 3 with at least two correct and no extras or Correct method to find sum of all three profits with at least two of 30, −15 or 20 correct. May work in pence but need to be consistent. Allow awrt 24.5 or 0.245
- M1d: Dep on previous method for finding profit for 500 rods. May work in pence but need to be consistent. Allow"0.2446..."$\times500$ or"their income" for 500 rods $-500\times0.2$ (accept 499 or 501)
- A1: All previous marks must be awarded for awrt 122 awrt 12200p. NB if uses any integer values for numbers of rods then it is A0 other than for 18 for $L > 8.09$

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The same manufacturer makes metal hinges in large batches.
The hinges each have a probability of 0.015 of having a fault.
A random sample of 200 hinges is taken from each batch and the batch is accepted if fewer than 6 hinges are faulty.
The manufacturer's aim is for 95% of batches to be accepted.

(d) Explain whether the manufacturer is likely to achieve its aim.
(4)

(d) Let $X \sim \mathrm{B}(200, 0.015)$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 5) = $ M1 or $\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 6) = $ M1

Manufacturer is unlikely to achieve their aim since $0.9176 < 0.95$ A1ft or Manufacturer is unlikely to achieve their aim since $0.0824 > 0.05$ A1ft
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Selecting the appropriate model. May be seen or used. Allow B(200,0.985) or Po(3) Condone B(0.015, 200) or B( 0.985, 200).
- M1: Writing or using $\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant5)$ Do not accept $\mathrm{P}(X<6)$ unless found $\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant5)$ / Writing or using $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant6)$ Do not accept $\mathrm{P}(X>5)$ unless found $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant6)$. A1: 0.92 (Poisson 0.916…) / 0.08 or better
- A1ft: Need at least one of the method marks to be awarded. Correct conclusion with the comparison (may be in words). Ft "their $p = 0.9176$…" as long as $p > 0.9$ If "their 0.9176…"< 0.95 must … be unlikely… If "their 0.9176…"> 0.95 they must say … be likely... To ft the alternative then $p < 0.1$

questions.stem: Dian uses the large data set to investigate the Daily Total Rainfall, $r\,\mathrm{mm}$, for Camborne.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down how a value of $0 < r \leqslant 0.05$ is recorded in the large data set.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) tr B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1: Allow Tr or trace or Trace
parts.notes: The mark scheme answer 'tr' (trace) refers to the large data set's recording convention; this is not a numbered spec statement itself but falls under the 'other_requirements' large-data-set familiarity requirement, so S2.4 (data recording/cleaning) is the closest content statement.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Dian uses the data for the 31 days of August 2015 for Camborne and calculates the following statistics

$n=31 \qquad \sum r = 174.9 \qquad \sum r^2 = 3523.283$

(b) Use these statistics to calculate
(i) the mean of the Daily Total Rainfall in Camborne for August 2015,
(ii) the standard deviation of the Daily Total Rainfall in Camborne for August 2015.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(i) $\mu = \dfrac{174.9}{31} = 5.6419\ldots$ awrt 5.64 B1
(ii) $\sigma_r = \sqrt{\dfrac{3523.283}{31} - \mu^2}$ M1
$= 9.04559\ldots$ awrt 9.05 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (ii) M1: For a correct expression for sd including the $\sqrt{\ }$ Ft their mean. A1: awrt 9.05 (Allow $s = 9.1932$… awrt 9.19) NB awrt to 9.05 or 9.19 with no working is M1 A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Dian believes that the mean Daily Total Rainfall in August is less in the South of the UK than in the North of the UK.
The mean Daily Total Rainfall in Leuchars for August 2015 is $1.72\,\mathrm{mm}$ to 2 decimal places.

(c) State, giving a reason, whether this provides evidence to support Dian's belief.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Leuchars is in the North and Camborne is in the South M1
The mean is smaller for Leuchars than Camborne therefore there is no evidence that Dian's belief is true A1ft
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: For stating Leuchars is North of Camborne oe eg Camborne is further south. A1ft: M1 must be awarded. A correct conclusion and correct comment about the means ft their mean in (b) Allow No
- SC for No and there are only 2 places used so there is insufficient data. Mark as M0A1 on epen

Dian uses the large data set to estimate the proportion of days with no rain in Camborne for 1987 to be 0.27 to 2 decimal places.

(d) Explain why the distribution $\mathrm{B}(14, 0.27)$ might not be a reasonable model for the number of days without rain for a 14-day summer event.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) eg $p=0.27$ is unlikely to be constant. B1

- B1: A correct reason referring to • independence (needs context as to what is independent) eg consecutive 14 days unlikely to be independent. • probability [of rain] not being constant. • Allow a comment that conveys the idea that the proportion of days with no rain will be different over the year.

questions.stem:
A dentist knows from past records that 10% of customers arrive late for their appointment.
A new manager believes that there has been a change in the proportion of customers who arrive late for their appointment.
A random sample of 50 of the dentist's customers is taken.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down

$\bullet$ a null hypothesis corresponding to no change in the proportion of customers who arrive late
$\bullet$ an alternative hypothesis corresponding to the manager's belief
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\mathrm{H_0}: p = 0.1$ $\mathrm{H_1}: p \neq 0.1$ B1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1: For both hypotheses in terms of $p$ or $\pi$. Connected to $\mathrm{H_0}$ and $\mathrm{H_1}$ correctly Condone 10% but not 10

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Using a 5% level of significance, find the critical region for a two-tailed test of the null hypothesis in (a)
You should state the probability of rejection in each tail, which should be less than 0.025
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Use of $X \sim \mathrm{B}(50, 0.1)$
implied by sight of one of awrt 0.0052 or awrt 0.9755 or awrt 0.0245 M1

$X=0$ and $X \geqslant 10$ plus $\mathrm{P}(X=0) = $ awrt 0.0052 and $\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 10) = $ awrt 0.0245 A1
SC: Both CR correct with no probabilities and no distribution seen scores M0A10
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Using correct distribution to find the probability associated with one tail of the CR If the correct distribution is stated (may be seen in part(a)) allow for one tail of the correct CR or one of (awrt 0.025 or awrt 0.005 or awrt 0.975) seen connected to a correct probability statement
- A1: Lower CR $X = 0$ / $X < 1$ / $X\leqslant0$ [condone eg P($X$ = 0) labelled as CR] Or Upper CR $X\geqslant10$ or $X > 9$ [condone $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant10)$ oe labelled as CR]. A1: Both CR's correct with the relevant probabilities Allow $\cup$ for "and" and $X > 9$, $X < 1$, $X\leqslant0$ [do not allow P($X$ = 0) or $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant10)$ oe] Allow CR in different form eg (9, $\infty$), [10,$\infty$)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the actual level of significance of the test based on your critical region from part (b)
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) 0.0297 B1ft
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1ft: awrt 0.0297 or 2.97% or ft for the sum of the probabilities in (b) for "their 2 critical regions" if seen. If none seen it must be awrt 0.0297
- SC M0 in (b) for a one tail test Allow B1ft for their one tail CR in (b) eg 0.0338 or 0.0245 or 0.0579

(1)
